Now I have the full picture.

## Login
No real authentication exists. **`frontend/src/app/services/auth.service.ts`**: `AuthService.login(username)` just looks up (or creates) a `UserProfile` in `localStorage` under `ai_dnd_user_<username>` (plus a pointer key `ai_dnd_user`) and sets an in-memory signal (`_profile`). `isLoggedIn()` just checks that signal is non-null. **`login.component.ts`** calls this and routes to `/characters` (new game) or shows saved campaign slots.

## Campaign storage
"Campaigns" are purely a client-side concept — `CampaignSlot[]` array inside `UserProfile` (`frontend/src/app/models/game.models.ts`), persisted only in browser `localStorage` (no server table for campaigns). Each slot stores `sessionId`/`characterId` pointers. The actual game state lives server-side: Workers KV holds the session (`worker/src/services/session.ts`, `loadSession`/`saveSession`), and D1's `characters` table (`worker/migrations/0001_initial_schema.sql`) holds the persistent character.

## Deleting a campaign slot
`login.component.ts` → `deleteCampaign()` → `AuthService.removeCampaign(slotId)` just filters the slot out of the local `UserProfile.campaigns` array and re-persists it to `localStorage`. **It never calls the backend** — there is no DELETE route for sessions or characters anywhere in `worker/src/routes/*`. So the server-side character row in D1 and its KV session are **not deleted**; they remain orphaned (still reachable via `GET /api/session/:id` or `GET /api/character/:id` if the old sessionId/characterId is known) until the KV session's TTL expires naturally.
